speaker: Doctor
text: The blood tests show a significant elevation in your white blood cell count, indicating an active infection. Since your wrist X-ray images are unavailable, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or swelling specifically around the wrist joint, and have you had any recent insect bites or minor injuries there?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the self-resolving knee pain last week, have you noticed any rash, particularly on your palms, soles, or buttocks, or any swollen lymph nodes in your neck or armpits?

REQUEST TEST: Syphilis Serology (RPR/FTA-ABS), Lyme Disease Serology, and Erythema Migrans photo.

Based on your history of self-resolving knee pain and recent camping in Minnesota, followed by this wrist infection and systemic symptoms, is the rash you mentioned earlier petechial (small red spots) or target-like?

REQUEST TEST: Erythema Chromicum Migrans (ECM) assessment, Joint Aspiration (Left Wrist), and Two-Spot Agglutination.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ECM assessment: Not available; Joint Aspiration (Left Wrist): Analysis - WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram Stain - Gram-negative diplococci seen; Two-Spot Agglutination: Not available.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The joint aspiration showing a markedly elevated white blood cell count and Gram-negative diplococci is highly specific for gonococcal arthritis. Given your history of sexual activity and the presence of fever and skin lesions, do you have any other joint pain or drainage from your urethra?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection.
